favourite.heading: Why Massachusetts can pull away
bullets: Massachusetts is the better football team by 8.4 points on opponent-adjusted results — but about 86% of that rating is still last season carried forward, and in a portal era last season is a different team (+8.4 pts).
Playing at Massachusetts is worth 4.1 points — the league-wide home-field number, because a per-venue table was tested and could not be told apart from the home team’s own quality (+4.1 pts).

underdog.heading: Why Sacred Heart can keep it close
bullets: The outcome range is 15.5 points wide at one sigma — p10 -11.6 to p90 +33.4 for Massachusetts, so a projection of +12.4 still produces results a long way either side of it.
It is early enough that both ratings still lean on preseason belief — it widens the outcome range by about 6%.
70% of the model’s own input contract was empty for this game — no starter, injury, schedule or per-player talent context reached it, so the number leans on team strength more than it should.
Sacred Heart is not in the FBS rating set, so EdgeDesk cannot measure what it does well. An unmeasured opponent is an unknown, not a weak one, and the size of the gap is not established.
